summary.text: Thetford permanent RV toilets (Aqua-Magic VI, Bravura, Aqua-Magic Residence, Aqua-Magic Style II, Style Plus and China Bowl) are pedal-flush toilets: pressing the pedal halfway adds water and all the way flushes. They have no display; the owner's manual troubleshoots by symptom: leaks, a bowl that will not hold water, a stiff pedal and a poor flush.

models.text: The permanent RV toilet owner's manual covers Aqua-Magic VI, Bravura, Aqua-Magic Residence, Aqua-Magic Style II, Aqua-Magic Style Plus and China Bowl; removing the product ID/serial number label can void the warranty.
A toilet's data tag is generally on the back of the toilet (a tight fit to reach), but on some models it is on the base.
Without a data tag, Thetford identifies a toilet from photos plus: hand, foot or wall-panel flush; lever or electric button; one or two pedals and their position; porcelain or plastic bowl.
On a cassette toilet the serial number label is usually near where you remove the tank, and there is also a serial number on both the cassette and the tank.
models.locator: FAQ 'Where is the serial number located on my cassette toilet?'

models.text: The serial number is required for all warranty claims, along with the proof of purchase.
A permanent toilet uses gravity to move waste into the holding tank; a macerating toilet uses a pump with a macerator. All Thetford toilets are tested up to 350 lbs / 159 kg.
models.locator: FAQ 'Is a permanent toilet the same as a macerator toilet?'

display.text: Pedal operation: press the pedal halfway to add water; press it all the way to flush.
Holding tanks: empty the waste holding tank when the level indicator shows full.
display.locator: FAQ 'When do I empty the waste holding tank?'

display.text: Sensors that always read 2/3 full can have different causes; Level Gauge Cleaner restores sensors that fail from tissue and sludge build-up, but not every sensor issue.
display.locator: FAQ 'holding tank sensors always reading 2/3 full'

display.text: On a cassette toilet, a worn lip seal, the rubber seal between toilet and waste tank, lets odours escape from the waste tank.

checks.text: Leak at back of toilet: check the water supply line connection at the water valve and secure or tighten it as necessary.
Leak between closet flange and toilet: check the flange nuts for tightness first.

Toilet does not hold water: Thetford Premium RV Slide-Out Rubber Seal Conditioner often corrects it; remove debris from the blade/ball seal track and check blade/ball seal compression with the mechanism.
Difficult pedal: use Thetford Toilet Seal Lubricant and Conditioner on the blade/ball; do not use petroleum-based lubricants.
Poor flush that persists: the manual says to check the supply flow rate, which should be at least 2.5 gallons per minute through a 3/8 inch inner-diameter supply line.
Cleaning: do not use petroleum-based products, scouring powders, acids or concentrated cleaners, which can damage surfaces, plastic parts and rubber seals and can void the warranty.
Bleach and acids in most household cleaners can dry out and damage seals; mild organic acids and citric acid do not. Household bowl-cleaner acids dull and pit the bowl.
Winterizing: when blowing water from the lines with air pressure, make sure the toilet valve is open; use RV (potable) antifreeze only, never automotive antifreeze.
Winterizing steps: turn off water supply, drain the bowl, disconnect the supply line at the water valve, drain the supply line, add antifreeze and 1/4 bottle of Toilet Seal Lubricant to the bowl.
Never leave the black tank dump valve open during use, even on a sewer hookup; liquids drain and leave solids that cause odors and clogs. The grey valve can stay open.
checks.locator: FAQ 'Can I leave my dump valves open'

checks.text: Holding tank contents can freeze; use RV antifreeze in both black and grey tanks. It is compatible with all Thetford holding tank products.
checks.locator: FAQ 'Will my holding tank contents freeze?'

checks.text: Do not travel with water in the flush tank, to prevent water damage to the vehicle (for example the C400 bench cassette toilet).
If an SC or CW cassette toilet will not flush, troubleshoot its direct connection to the RV freshwater tank.
Cassette toilets: keep the blade valve closed when not in use, rinse the tank after every empty, and lubricate the lip seal twice a season.
A leaking cassette waste tank: first check that the tank is positioned properly and that the lip seal is intact.

parts.text: Named parts include vacuum breaker, flush nozzle, mechanism assembly, closet flange seal and bolts, water module/water valve, blade seal, waste ball, pedal and cable packages. A failed vacuum breaker means replacing the whole assembly.
A leak behind the toilet is most likely a bad vacuum breaker, which needs to be replaced.
If the water valve keeps leaking, replace it; if the vacuum breaker leaks while flushing, replace the vacuum breaker or water module, depending on model; replace a worn blade/ball seal.
Flange leak that continues after tightening: remove the toilet, check flange height, shim with Thetford spacers to 7/16 inch above floor if needed, and replace the flange seal.
Thetford recommends replacing the cassette lip seal every four to six years, depending on use.
Aqua-Magic V service kits include blade seal (also fits VI), mechanism repair package, replacement flush pedal, pedal cable and nozzle assembly.
A leaking waste holding tank is fixed by replacing the tank.
parts.locator: FAQ 'What can I do when my waste holding tank is leaking?'

callTech.text: For parts or service, contact a local Thetford Certified Service Center or an RV dealer. For warranty, call Thetford Customer Service with name and address, model and serial number, problem description and proof of purchase date.
Warranty parts and service go through a Thetford/Norcold Authorized Service Center or RV dealer; Thetford replaces or repairs toilets or parts and pays the authorized dealer for warranty labor.
callTech.locator: FAQ 'What should I do if I have a warranty claim?'

callTech.text: If water is frozen in the toilet, do not attempt to flush until the ice thaws.
